  "title": "Decision on Airstrike Against Potential Taliban Group When Civilian Presence Uncertain",
  "setting": "Gerani Village, Bala Balouk District, Farah Province, Afghanistan, 4 May 2009, U.S. Central Command operation",
  "decider": "ground force commander",
  "agent_recast": false,
  "recast_note": "",
  "agent": "ground force commander",
  "agent_role": "decide",
  "situation": "The ground force was under direct enemy fire and awaiting a medical evacuation helicopter. A B-1B bomber observed a group of similarly sized adults moving tactically across difficult terrain behind the enemy front line. Real‑time intelligence indicated the group's location and movement matched Taliban orders to mass and re‑attack friendly forces, leading the commander to assess an imminent threat. The commander directed the B-1B to strike the group and a building they entered, despite the crew being unable to confirm whether civilians were present. Subsequent investigation found that the first strike caused no civilian deaths, but later strikes likely resulted in civilian casualties and did not fully follow controlling guidance.",
  "question": "What should the ground force commander do regarding striking the groups assessed as massing Taliban fighters, including the building, when civilian presence cannot be confirmed?",

    {
      "id": "F10",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "confirmed",

    }
